hero.eyebrow: From permit file to visualization booklet
hero.lead: Upload your permit files, DXF, DWG, PDF or DWF, and get a complete visualization booklet with a certificate that measures every wall against the sheet. No manual drafting, no revision rounds.
hero.ctaPrimary: Upload a file, get a booklet
hero.dragHint: Drag the line: the sheet and the render align to the centimetre

stats.stepsLabel: steps, with a live progress meter

how.title: Seven steps. You see every one of them.
how.lead: The system reads the files, builds a model, renders, checks itself and assembles a booklet. At any moment you see which step the job is in, how much was scanned and how long is left.
how.s1Body: Drop a whole folder: plans, elevations, sections and survey.
how.s2Body: Each sheet gets a role by its content. See how much was scanned, and what was not read and why.
how.s3Body: One form, only for what the files do not answer. Every question has a default.
how.s4Body: A credit estimate and a ceiling before you start. You are charged only for a delivered booklet.
how.s5Body: A 3D model from the file's geometry, and a render for every view.
how.s6Body: Overlay against the sheet, cameras, materials, and render-versus-painting comparison.
how.s7Body: Painted renders, plans, an assumptions page and an accuracy certificate, ready to submit.

accuracy.title: Not "looks similar". Measured.
accuracy.lead: Every booklet ships with a certificate that measures two links separately: the model against the sheet, in metres, and the painting against the render it was painted from, in pixels. A painting that drifted does not enter the booklet; the exact render goes in instead.
accuracy.legal: The certificate measures geometric agreement with the uploaded files. It is not a check of permit or regulatory compliance.

reads.title: Everything drawn goes in. What was not read is named.
reads.lead: Rules learned from dozens of real projects: sales flats, private houses, public buildings, a synagogue and an industrial plant.
reads.wallsBody: From layers, hatches and geometry, even when layers are non-standard.
reads.openingsBody: From door swings in the plan, matched to the elevations.
reads.levelsBody: From level marks and sections, including design versus survey levels.
reads.surveyBody: Survey codes from the legend, terrain, roads, fences and trees.
reads.furnitureBody: By room type and building type: flat, office, plant or synagogue.
reads.proposalsBody: Two proposals in one file become one booklet with a comparison.
reads.rescanBody: Complementary readers look for what the first scan missed, and show the difference.

privacy.title: Your files stay yours.
privacy.body: The permit form strip with names and ID numbers is never read. Files are deleted after delivery under a policy you choose.
privacy.localBody: The same system, installed on your computer. Files never leave the office.

pricing.title: One annual subscription. Credits by usage.
pricing.inc2: Every building type and file format
pricing.inc3: An accuracy certificate in every booklet
pricing.inc5: Buy extra credits at any time
pricing.note: Credits are charged only for a delivered booklet.

faq.q1: What if a sheet is missing?
faq.a1: The system uses a default and marks it on the booklet's assumptions page. If no sensible default exists, it stops before charging and says exactly what is missing.
faq.q2: And if the painting invents something?
faq.a2: A drift gate compares every painting to its render. A painting that moved is replaced by the exact render, and the certificate records it.
faq.q3: Do I need to prepare the files?
faq.a3: No. Upload what was submitted for the permit. The system recognises each office's layers and learns them.
faq.a4: It depends on the project's size. The progress meter shows an estimate from the first moment, and you can close the page and get a notification.
